idiom_name: plain object or small class over a Map satisfying the collaborator's shape
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no interface declarations, so the fake is simply an object (or a small class) exposing the same methods over a Map, and nothing of the classic structure has to be built. Install it through the code under test's constructor or a factory, and avoid module-level stores so every test gets a fresh one. When the collaborator is an HTTP service, an in-process fake server plays the same role at a different seam, while jest.mock/vi.mock module substitution is a heavier global seam to prefer only when the code imports the collaborator directly.
pitfalls: A module-level store shared by every test leaks writes between tests - return a fresh fake per test instead.
An object literal silently misses methods when the collaborator grows; add a TypeScript interface or a contract test against the real collaborator.
A fake that answers synchronously where the real client returns a Promise makes the suite green and production broken - keep the async shape.
